headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,062 AS BARRICK BEAT ABSORBS — CPI WEDNESDAY IS THE NEXT BINARY FOR THE $4,000 FLOOR
snippet: Gold opened the November 9 session at $4,062/oz and silver at $51.61 — holding the range established after Barrick's Q3 beat — with the focus now shifting from earnings to Wednesday's CPI print as the next macro catalyst capable of breaking gold out of or down from its current $3,990–$4,100 band. The Warsh Fed's hawkish stance means a hot print could suppress the upside; a soft print clears the technical resistance and sets up the $4,100 test junior gold investors have been anticipating.

headline: FIREFLY METALS DRILLS 16.4M @ 9.2% CUEQ AT MING MINE — GREEN BAY EXPANDS BEYOND AUGUST RESOURCE BOUNDARY
snippet: FireFly Metals (ASX/TSX: FFM) reported November 9 that underground drilling at the Ming Mine in Newfoundland's Green Bay copper district hit up-dip mineralisation outside the August 2026 Mineral Resource Estimate — the best hole returning 16.4 metres at 9.2% copper-equivalent, extending the high-grade core zone laterally and demonstrating that the August resource boundary understates the deposit's current extent. For TSX-V and ASX copper investors, FireFly's Green Bay is one of the highest-grade undeveloped copper systems in a stable Western jurisdiction, and results like this keep the discovery-to-resource upgrade cycle in play.

headline: TOP 50 MINERS SHED $264 BILLION AS AI-GOLD TRADE UNWINDS, LITHIUM NAMES EXIT INDEX
snippet: Mining.com's latest Top 50 ranking found the world's biggest mining companies collectively shed $264 billion in market capitalisation as the AI-linked gold narrative unwound in the October–November 2026 selloff, with lithium producers SQM, Albemarle and Ganfeng dropping below the index threshold as the cycle low narrows the gap to exit. For retail junior mining investors, the pullback in senior producer multiples is a leading indicator: historically, when large-cap gold majors re-rate down from peak AI-driven premiums, the valuation gap between seniors and TSX-V juniors compresses — which can accelerate M&A activity as majors look to buy growth at discount.

headline: ANDEAN SILVER HITS HIGH-GRADE VEINS 1KM FROM CERRO BAYO PLANT — 136MOZ RESOURCE OPEN IN ALL DIRECTIONS
snippet: Andean Silver (ASX: ASL) reported new high-grade silver-gold vein discoveries approximately one kilometre from the existing Cerro Bayo processing plant in Chilean Patagonia, with the mineralised zones open along strike and at depth — strengthening the case for a resource update expected in the first half of 2027 to expand the current 136 million silver-equivalent ounce estimate. Near-plant discoveries carry immediate economic weight that greenfield finds do not, and with silver holding above $51/oz, Cerro Bayo's existing infrastructure creates a capital efficiency story rarely available to exploration-stage companies.

headline: COPPER CLAWS BACK POST-MIDTERM LOSSES AS PHYSICAL DEMAND HOLDS — PAPER MARKET RECOVERING FROM 10-WEEK LOW
snippet: LME copper clawed back a portion of its post-midterm losses as markets opened November 9, with the paper market recovering from a 10-week low as AI-spending fears that drove the selloff began to fade — while physical demand indicators, led by last week's record Yangshan copper premium, confirmed that real-world tightness had not abated during the futures weakness. For TSX-V and ASX copper juniors, the divergence between a physical market at decade-high tightness and a paper market pricing macro sentiment argues for patience over capitulation in the current pullback.

headline: CHINA GREENLIGHTS LITHIUM HYDROXIDE FUTURES — PRICE DISCOVERY LANDMARK FOR BATTERY SUPPLY CHAIN
snippet: China's securities regulator approved registration of lithium hydroxide futures and options contracts, adding a formal exchange-traded price-discovery mechanism for battery-grade lithium hydroxide — the refined form required by most EV cathode manufacturers — to the country that dominates both lithium hydroxide refining and global battery manufacturing. For junior lithium developers on the TSX-V and ASX negotiating offtake agreements with downstream partners, the new futures contract creates a more transparent and auditable reference price, potentially reducing the information asymmetry that has historically disadvantaged smaller producers in long-term supply contract negotiations.

headline: LODE RESOURCES ACHIEVES 99% PURE ANTIMONY FROM TASMANIA — SCOPING STUDY ADVANCING AT MONTEZUMA
snippet: Lode Resources (ASX: LDR) reported laboratory-scale production of antimony metal at 99–99.5% purity from its Montezuma project in Tasmania, meeting the specification threshold for defence and flame-retardant applications as the company advances a scoping study on the deposit. Antimony was added to both U.S. and EU critical mineral lists in 2024, and China's export control actions in late 2024 triggered a supply chain scramble that has yet to be fully resolved — making Western-jurisdiction antimony projects like Montezuma strategically relevant to downstream buyers regardless of their scale, and the purity result is a key derisker for future off-take discussions.

headline: GOLD CPI SETUP: WHAT WEDNESDAY'S INFLATION PRINT MEANS FOR THE $4,000 FLOOR AFTER THE MIDTERM REBOUND
snippet: Commodity analysts writing November 9 morning frame Wednesday's U.S. CPI as the first real stress test for gold's post-midterm recovery — with the metal near $4,066 after a 4.8% weekly gain and $3,990 identified as the floor junior gold investors should monitor for a potential breakdown signal if CPI comes in soft and dollar strength resumes. The competing scenario where inflation remains sticky reinforces gold's safe-haven case even under a hawkish Warsh Fed, and several analysts argue sticky CPI would be more bullish for gold than a soft print that benefits equities broadly.

headline: RUSSIA TIGHTENING URANIUM GRIP: 44% OF GLOBAL ENRICHMENT NOW, ON TRACK FOR 36% OF RESOURCES BY 2040
snippet: A Washington Times analysis citing a London-based energy think tank warns that Russia could control up to 36% of global uranium resources by 2040 while already holding approximately 44% of the world's uranium enrichment capacity — a combination that gives Moscow significant leverage over Western nuclear power programmes as governments accelerate reactor build-outs. For uranium sector investors, the analysis reinforces the structural supply argument for Western uranium developers: at the point where the U.S., EU, and allied governments are racing to build enrichment independence, the jurisdiction-security premium on stable Western uranium mining and conversion assets increases materially independent of the spot price.

headline: VALUATION GAP PERSISTS: FIVE GOLD MINERS YET TO CLOSE ON $4,000+ GOLD PRICE — WHAT CLOSES IT
snippet: Yahoo Finance identifies five gold mining stocks where the gap between current equity valuations and the implied NPV of their production economics at sustained $4,000+ gold prices has not yet closed — framing the analysis around the persistent underperformance of mining equities relative to the gold price itself that has characterised 2026. The analysis argues that M&A activity or institutional capital rotation from physical gold ETF exposure toward equity leverage on the gold price are the two likeliest mechanisms for closing the gap, and that Barrick's strong Q3 delivered precisely the proof-of-concept that institutional allocators were waiting for before rotating.
